title: Stage D: ruling pencil |F| on F_e needs effective Picard data, not just numerics

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Stage D / Remark `rem:terminal`: extracting the ruling pencil $|F|$ on $\mathbb{F}_e$ requires an effective Picard/divisor-class computation that is not provided.**

`rem:terminal` extracts the ruling class $F$ ($F^2=0$, $F\cdot K=-2$) by "solving the numerical conditions in $\mathrm{NS}(\mathbb{F}_e)=\mathbb{Z}C_0\oplus\mathbb{Z}F$" and then taking $H^0(\mathcal{O}(F))$. But the algorithm only has $S_{\min}$ as an ideal in $\mathbb{P}^M$. To compute $H^0(\mathcal{O}_S(F))$ one must first realize the abstract class $F$ by an actual effective divisor / line bundle on the given model -- an effective divisor-class membership problem. Knowing the intersection numbers $F^2,F\cdot K$ does **not** by itself give the sections.

This is the same kind of effective-$\mathrm{Pic}$ computation the solution deliberately avoids in the $\mathbb{P}^2$ sub-case (where it instead blows up a $k$-point to get $\mathbb{F}_1$). For genuine $\mathbb{F}_e$ with $e\ge 2$ no such workaround is given, so the ruling is not made effective.

**Repair.** Recover the ruling either (a) from the explicit blow-down history that produced $S_{\min}$ (which gives an explicit $\mathrm{NS}$ basis with effective representatives), or (b) by an effective algorithm computing $H^0$ of the relevant line bundle from a known divisor in the class (e.g. a fiber of the conic-bundle map), not merely from numerical conditions.
